scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - the edge layer's error envelope is not machine-readable, and it is not shaped like the db layer's. Two concrete defects, both measured against the local edge runtime this session: (1) an edge function's error body is {"error": "<prose>"} with NO machine-readable `code` field, so a caller can only pattern-match English to decide what happened - while the SAME platform's db layer returns {code, details, hint, message} for every failure class (400 bad column, 404 unknown table, 401 no grant), which a client CAN branch on. One product, two incompatible error contracts. (2) a routing 404 (unknown function name) is returned as **text/plain**, so `res.json()` THROWS rather than yielding an error object - the caller's catch block sees a SyntaxError about unexpected token, not a 404, and any code that checks `data.error` never runs. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the layer behind the AI gateway, the orchestrators, OCR/voice capture and report generation. A client that treats db and edge errors alike - which the identical-looking `.error` property invites - will mishandle one of them, and the failure mode is the one this bank keeps finding: an exception swallowed into an empty render, indistinguishable from a server that honestly answered nothing. LEFT OWED RATHER THAN GREEN, DELIBERATELY: the oracle asks that status and body AGREE and that the envelope be uniform, and it does not. Banking it green would be a false green; recording it owed with the diagnosis is the honest state. findings.title: QUALIFIED - invalid-but-present enum returns 200 (analytics-orchestrator accepts any phase)
findings.detail: QUALIFIED BY A LATER MEASUREMENT IN THE SAME SESSION - flagged rather than left standing. This row was banked on four edge probes: 400 naming a missing field, 400 from a second function naming a different missing field, 404 for an unknown function, and 200 for a successful run. That evidence holds. But it did NOT include an INVALID-BUT-PRESENT field value, and probing that afterwards found analytics-orchestrator returns 200 for ANY phase string - metrics, analyze, summary, phase1 all returned 200 with the invalid phase ECHOED BACK, plus period_days:90 and a generated_at, even though the function's own source recognises only report, descriptive, diagnostic, predictive and prescriptive. So `phase` is validated for PRESENCE and never for VALIDITY. WHY THAT BEARS ON THIS ORACLE: a 200 returning a result for an input the function does not recognise is a response whose status claims success for a request that was not actually understood. My banked wording said 'no 200-carrying-an-error', which was true of the cases I probed and is not established for this one. I am recording the qualification rather than quietly leaving the green, because a row that a later measurement undercuts is exactly the drift this bank exists to prevent - and because the same session that earned the row found the counter-case. NOT WITHDRAWN, and the reasoning is stated so it can be overruled: the four probed cases genuinely agree, and the new case is better classified as an input-VALIDATION defect than a status/body disagreement - the body IS internally consistent with the 200 it carries. Whether an unvalidated enum should return 400 is a design call on the function, not a contradiction between its status and its body. If the next walk judges otherwise, withdraw this row with a false-green-withdrawn finding; the evidence for both readings is recorded here. TO FINISH: validate `phase` against the known set in analytics-orchestrator and return 400 naming the valid values (the function already returns 400 with a named field for absence, so the pattern exists); then re-probe the invalid-enum case and settle this row without a qualification. Per A15 no edit was made - the edit budget is closed and it belongs in the next batched wave.

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

withdrawn_evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA ON A MEASURED DENOMINATOR (rail R10). This page's 2 read relation(s) do not intersect the 40 probed at the gateway. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py - 80 unit-bearing quantity columns judged on whether their meaning is PINNED (a CHECK, a COMMENT, a sibling unit column, or a unit-bearing name) and whether their stored values agree with ONE scale.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_units_at_boundary.py - 80 unit-bearing quantity columns judged on whether their meaning is PINNED (a CHECK, a COMMENT, a sibling unit column, or a unit-bearing name) and whether their stored values agree with ONE scale. Platform: 73 declared | 2 UNDECLARED | 5 latent | 0 MIXED-SCALE. Zero mixed-scale is the load-bearing number: no column stores fractions and whole percents in the same place. FOR THIS LAYER THE QUESTION IS GENUINELY OPEN, AND IT IS THE ONE LAYER THE SCHEMA CANNOT ANSWER. Every other boundary here carries values whose meaning is pinned by the column they come from. An AI-EMITTED number is not from a column - it is generated, and nothing in the schema constrains whether it arrives as hours or days, pesos or credits, a fraction or a whole percent. That is precisely the confusion this oracle exists to catch, and it is the one place the structural argument used for the other layers does NOT transfer. Recorded as owed rather than passed by association. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: capture an AI-produced quantity from this page's own AI path and check the emitted value against the unit its consumer assumes - the same before/after discipline the other provers use, applied to a generated number rather than a stored one.

evidence.asserts: What one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS: a value is not silently rewritten on the way in by something nobody named. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - values_survive_write extracts every trigger that assigns to NEW, classifies the rewrite by its STRUCTURE, and fails on any that belongs to no named class. It also measures the one class that can lose a person's work: every left(NEW.col, N) cap is read against the stored data, because a possible truncation and an actual one are different facts.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). It earned that by first FAILING on a trigger I had added earlier in this same session: tg_community_posts_moderation_fields, which restores flagged/pinned for a caller who is not a supervisor of that hive (migrations ...000063/64, after a reported author was found clearing their own flag). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.

Most numbers on this platform are COUNTS - 9 open jobs, 28 PMs overdue - and a count has no unit to show; flagging those would redden every surface, and a check that reddens everything is measuring itself. findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. The prover now compares the row's captured JSON against its after-state for any capture case, which is what actually answers 'did the effect land'. ★THE WRITE DISCIPLINE HERE IS CAPTURE-AND-RESTORE, NOT CREATE-AND-DELETE, because there is no new row to remove and deleting the plan would leave the hive without the briefing it had before I arrived. Banking green on the DB half alone would be asserting the visible half from the invisible one, which is precisely the proxy error above. THE PREMISE WAS CHECKED FIRST, because filing this against a page that is guarded elsewhere would be a manufactured finding: utils.js already defines whRequireOnline(action, notify) and exposes it as window.whRequireOnline, and it already carries the exact sentence this oracle asks for - 'You are offline. <action> needs a connection - nothing was sent, so nothing is half-done.' The scanner's GUARD pattern matches RequireOnline( and navigator.onLine === false, so a page that called either would have counted as guarded. None of these writes call anything. This is NON-ADOPTION of a centralized, correctly-worded helper, not a missing message. WHY THE PLATFORM'S EXISTING GREEN DOES NOT COVER THIS: tools/validate_offline_write_guard.py PASSES at fail-severity, but its PAGES list is exactly ['marketplace.html', 'marketplace-seller.html'] - 19 writes on two pages. None of the 22 roster pages is in its scope, so its green says nothing about them. And widening that list alone would NOT be enough: the validator's user_invokable() recognises only window.X = and inline onclick/onchange/onsubmit, so of the 53 exposed writes measured across the roster it would see 37 and miss the 16 bound with addEventListener. WHAT A PASSIVE BANNER DOES NOT DO, since every page already adopts one: the banner states the condition, it does not refuse the action. The button still fires, the request still leaves, and the person still cannot tell whether their work landed - which is the whole distinction this oracle draws. THE FIX IS ONE LINE PER WRITE at the top of each function - if (!whRequireOnline('<gerund>', showToast)) return; - and the highest-stakes ones on this page should go first. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS after the guards land: prove it LIVE rather than statically, and note that setOffline does not flip navigator.onLine in the page, so the probe must override navigator.onLine AND block the network, then assert that zero requests fired and the sentence reached the person.

findings.detail: FAILS: with 2 reads answered 500, **no retry control is present** - zero visible elements whose label mentions retry or try-again. It also says nothing at all about the failure (245 visible characters). SO THE ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant costs the whole page again on the connection that just failed. THE PATTERN EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM, so this is adoption: achievements renders a Retry button beside its toast, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 post cards. Only 2 of 22 pages have one. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that RE-ISSUES the failed read - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. PLATFORM RESULT, all 22 pages: **9 state the failure in domain language** (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant) and **11 say nothing or assert a falsehood**. Only 2 offer a retry CONTROL (achievements, community); public-feed's was measured firing a real re-request and rendering 15 posts.

findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED DECISIVELY: **this page writes `0` into its KPI heroes while the reads are still pending**, then replaces them with real values once the data lands. With 6 reads in flight and **0 resolved**, the observer recorded 49 server-derived numeric writes, including `sb-risk-hero` = 0, `sb-pms-hero` = 0, `sb-carry-hero` = 0, `risk-count` = 0 and `pms-count` = 0. After resolution, 9 further writes landed - `risk-count` = 2 plus percentages of 77% and 74%. SO THOSE ZEROS ARE ASSERTIONS, NOT PLACEHOLDERS - the render reached the elements first and stamped a zero into them. That is the precise distinction three pages in this same wave passed on (voice-journal, public-feed and engineering-design wrote no server figure at all while waiting). THE STAKES HERE: shift-brain is the autonomous shift-planning surface, and the zeros it paints are `sb-risk-hero`, `sb-pms-hero` and `sb-carry-hero` - risk, PMs due, and carry-over. A supervisor opening the plan on a slow connection reads 'no risk, no PMs, nothing carried over' at the exact moment they are deciding what the shift does. The true risk count was 2. TO FINISH (batched per A15): do not write to those hero elements until the read resolves - hold the skeleton, or write the dash sentinel. alert-hub is the reference implementation on this platform: 6 skeleton elements and ZERO bare numbers during the wait. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver records every mutation whose text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that instant - so 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact rather than an inference. The probe writes its own sentinel ('4242') and the reading is REFUSED unless the observer sees it; all pages in this wave returned controlOK = true. THAT CONTROL EXISTS BECAUSE TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS PROBE LIED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION: one tested only the added node's own text (missing numeric leaves nested inside an innerHTML render), the other never attached at all because `document.documentElement` was null at init-script time. Both reported 0 writes on pages that visibly populated. A zero from an unattached observer is indistinguishable from an honest page. AND THE ORACLE IS NOT 'were numbers written' BUT 'were SERVER-DERIVED numbers written' - a page may honestly paint its own static or client-local figures while waiting. Writes to the offline-queue badge (`wh-conn-queue`, an IndexedDB depth the page owns without any read) and to decorative stage numerals are classified separately and excluded.

findings.title: LEFT OWED BECAUSE THIS VIEW HAS NO COMMITTING WRITE - recorded with the control named and its behaviour read, rather than passed on an empty denominator.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED BECAUSE THIS VIEW HAS NO COMMITTING WRITE - recorded with the control named and its behaviour read, rather than passed on an empty denominator. MEASURED FROM THE SOURCE: the verdict summary's single primary control is #sb-action-btn, and setCta() binds it as PURE NAVIGATION - `b.onclick = (e) => { e.preventDefault(); document.querySelector(scroll)?.scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth', block:'start'}); }`. It relabels itself to whatever the verdict recommends ('Inspect N risk assets', 'Clear N carry-forward') and scrolls to #risk-list or #carry-list. There is no insert, update, upsert, delete or writing rpc anywhere in this view. So the oracle - 'offline, the write is refused before firing and the person is told nothing was sent' - has nothing to grade here, and a green would be a pass over an empty denominator, which is exactly the false-green this bank exists to prevent. IT IS NOT declared-na EITHER, deliberately: R10 requires a reason AND a replacement, and the honest replacement is not obvious yet - this view's real obligations are that its verdict matches its own inputs and that its CTA scrolls to the list the recommendation is about, both of which belong to other oracles (CM what_is_this_number / CI domain-truth). Naming that is more useful than forcing a verdict. ★A COHORT OBSERVATION, because this is not one page's quirk: analytics, alert-hub and shift-brain render the SAME executive-summary chrome under three id prefixes (an- / ah- / sb-), each with -verdict, -verdict-label, -verdict-sub, three hero cards and an -action-btn. The roadmap already flags them as a shared-component cohort. If this CTA is navigation-only here, it is navigation-only there too - so analytics' and alert-hub's equivalent verdict-summary views inherit this same 'no committing write' conclusion, and none of the three should be graded for a refusal it cannot perform. Worth confirming on the other two before their rows are touched, but the shared implementation is the reason to expect it. WHAT THIS PAGE'S REAL OFFLINE WRITES ARE, all on V1 and already live-proven green: publishPlan (releases the plan to the crew under the supervisor's name) and archivePlan (withdraws a published plan from the crew's active view) - both guarded and both measured at ZERO shift_plans requests plus the refusal sentence.

observed.likely_replacement_oracles: CM what_is_this_number / CI domain-truth - the verdict must match its own inputs, and the CTA must scroll to the list it names
observed.cohort: analytics (an-), alert-hub (ah-) and shift-brain (sb-) share this executive-summary chrome; the same no-write conclusion should hold for their equivalent views - confirm before touching those rows

findings.detail: FAILS, MEASURED DECISIVELY: **this page writes `0` into its KPI heroes while the reads are still pending**, then replaces them with real values once the data lands. With 6 reads in flight and **0 resolved**, the observer recorded 49 server-derived numeric writes, including `sb-risk-hero` = 0, `sb-pms-hero` = 0, `sb-carry-hero` = 0, `risk-count` = 0 and `pms-count` = 0. After resolution, 9 further writes landed - `risk-count` = 2 plus percentages of 77% and 74%. SO THOSE ZEROS ARE ASSERTIONS, NOT PLACEHOLDERS - the render reached the elements first and stamped a zero into them. That is the precise distinction three pages in this same wave passed on (voice-journal, public-feed and engineering-design wrote no server figure at all while waiting). THE STAKES HERE: shift-brain is the autonomous shift-planning surface, and the zeros it paints are `sb-risk-hero`, `sb-pms-hero` and `sb-carry-hero` - risk, PMs due, and carry-over. A supervisor opening the plan on a slow connection reads 'no risk, no PMs, nothing carried over' at the exact moment they are deciding what the shift does. The true risk count was 2. TO FINISH (batched per A15): do not write to those hero elements until the read resolves - hold the skeleton, or write the dash sentinel. alert-hub is the reference implementation on this platform: 6 skeleton elements and ZERO bare numbers during the wait. MEASURED BY DETECTING THE WRITE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL. Reads are wrapped in a 5s delay and counted on resolution; a MutationObserver records every mutation whose text is purely numeric, stamped with how many reads had resolved at that instant - so 'did the page write a number before it had the data?' is a measured fact rather than an inference. The probe writes its own sentinel ('4242') and the reading is REFUSED unless the observer sees it; all pages in this wave returned controlOK = true. THAT CONTROL EXISTS BECAUSE TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS PROBE LIED IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION: one tested only the added node's own text (missing numeric leaves nested inside an innerHTML render), the other never attached at all because `document.documentElement` was null at init-script time. Both reported 0 writes on pages that visibly populated. A zero from an unattached observer is indistinguishable from an honest page. AND THE ORACLE IS NOT 'were numbers written' BUT 'were SERVER-DERIVED numbers written' - a page may honestly paint its own static or client-local figures while waiting. Writes to the offline-queue badge (`wh-conn-queue`, an IndexedDB depth the page owns without any read) and to decorative stage numerals are classified separately and excluded.

evidence.asserts: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible
evidence.checked: PASSES. WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): OBJECT-level access: the gate's cross-tenant READ and OWN-SCOPE WRITE checks - read_logbook_xhive and read_cxp_xhive (a FOREIGN hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows) and logbook_edit_ownscope (a member cannot UPDATE another hive's logbook entry). These are per-OBJECT refusals: the caller names a specific row they do not own and is refused, which is exactly what BOLA asks. Persona under test on this row: worker (may read, not generate) - and the gate's probe IS that persona, a real authenticated member of one hive reaching for another's data. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of those checks returning a row it should not, and the gate is known to fire because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught - 1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, and a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the instrument the platform already owns instead of writing another: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. Current result: 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS ROLE-CORRECT, which is the only reason it means anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims. A probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction - and that is not hypothetical, it cost a false finding on this very platform the same day, when an approved change order looked EDITABLE as `postgres` and is in fact refused for both a worker and a supervisor, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path. IT IS RESEED-ROBUST: the actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot quietly turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the WRONG reason and read as a pass. AND IT CARRIES NO-REGRESSION CHECKS (join_rpc_ok, founder_create_ok), so a gate that 'passed' by breaking the legitimate path would be caught rather than celebrated. WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE: it was hand-walked in an earlier session and banked with no `evidence.replay`, so nothing could re-earn it without a human repeating the whole probe. It now carries the command, which is the entire point of the A16 anti-stale discipline: 546 db-anchored rows on this platform are in exactly that position, and this is 176 of them coming out of it.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

findings.title: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (2 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.title: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it.
findings.detail: NOT BANKED, BECAUSE THE PASS IS VACUOUS ON THIS VIEW - and the prover's own numbers are what show it. tools/prove_dialog_a11y.mjs graded 36 of 43 registry targets with ZERO failing, and its summary line reads 'every focusable control shows a causally-verified focus indicator'. On this view that sentence is true the way any statement about an empty set is true: the report records focus.candidates = 0 and focus.checked = 0. No focusable control was examined, so nothing about focus indication was established. Banking it green would put a row in the bank whose evidence is an empty denominator - the exact false green this bank exists to prevent. THIS IS A PROPERTY OF THE VIEW, NOT A DEFECT. Six of the thirty-six graded views hold no focusable controls at all - engineering-design's guide tab, shift-brain's verdict summary and its details disclosure, report-sender's contacts list, public-feed's feed list, achievements' recent list. They are READ surfaces: text, cards and figures. A view with nothing to focus cannot fail a focus oracle, and it cannot pass one either. WORTH SEPARATING FROM THE SIBLING ORACLES, because they are NOT vacuous here: this same run measured accessible names and reduced-motion on the same views and those are real readings - a name applies to any control, focusable or not, and 'nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion' is a statement about the whole subtree. So the a11y run is only empty for FOCUS on these six. WHAT WOULD SETTLE THIS ROW: either the view genuinely gains an interactive control (then re-run and grade it), or the row is dispositioned declared-na with this reason under R10 - which needs a replacement oracle named, and the honest replacement is that the view is READABLE and its figures are labelled (CL contrast + CM what_is_this_number), not that its focus ring works. AND AN INSTRUMENT NOTE, since the prover is otherwise strong: its per-view PASS does not distinguish 'checked N controls, all good' from 'checked none'. The distinction is recoverable only from focus.candidates in the report, so a consumer that reads the exit code alone would bank all six of these as proven. The count belongs in the printed line.

observed.verdict: vacuous - no focusable control exists on this view, so the oracle is neither passed nor failed
observed.siblings_are_real: accessible-name and reduced-motion readings on this same view are NOT vacuous
observed.views_in_this_class: 6 of 36 graded - engineering-design V3, shift-brain V2 + V3, report-sender V2, public-feed V3, achievements V2
observed.instrument_note: the printed PASS does not distinguish 'checked N, all good' from 'checked none'; only focus.candidates reveals it
observed.to_settle: gain a real interactive control and re-run, or disposition declared-na with a replacement oracle (readability + labelled figures)

evidence.asserts: keyboard focus is visible on every interactive element, including custom ones
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_dialog_a11y.mjs: {"targets": 43, "graded": 35, "ungraded": 8, "failing": 0} - every control has an accessible name, every focusable control shows a CAUSALLY-VERIFIED focus indicator, and nothing animates under prefers-reduced-motion (spinners exempt and counted). ★'CAUSALLY VERIFIED' IS THE LOAD-BEARING WORD: the ring is read after a REAL Tab keypress lands on the control, because :focus-visible applies only to keyboard focus - asserting it from CSS would credit a ring a keyboard user never sees. And where a Tab walk reaches nothing inside a non-trapping dialog, focus is SEEDED ON THE CONTAINER and the walk repeated, with `seeded` recorded, because three views once reported 'candidates: 2, checked: 0, noRing: []' - a green summary over a walk that examined nothing. FOR THIS PAGE: 2 dialog view(s) walked. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

findings.title: FAILS: with 9 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 4370 characters before the refusal and 755 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than ID
findings.detail: FAILS: with 9 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 4370 characters before the refusal and 755 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. The platform already has the pieces - a central WRITE-failure message and the correct 401-vs-403 discriminator in utils.js - but there is no equivalent on the READ path, so a refused read renders as dashes or blanks with no explanation. On logbook the numbers '516 entries 30 machines 6 open' became '- entries - machines - open' with the body text identical to the character (1107 before and after) and not one word about why. A person cannot tell 'there is no data' from 'the load failed' from 'you are not allowed', and those three call for three different actions. THE FIX IS ONE ADOPTION, not 15 edits: give the read path the same treatment the write path already has. This independently reproduces a finding already recorded as 'the message already exists; the gap is ADOPTION on the read path'. SCOPE: V1, the page as it loads, and READ refusal only - a refused WRITE is a different path with its own central message, and is not claimed here. 5 of the 22 pages are excluded from the sweep because they are public or have no authenticated read to refuse. The walk is NON-WRITING.

evidence.asserts: after a re-run, the surface names what changed and what is still owed
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK with the orchestrator answered by a faithful payload - the page treats any data.error as failure and otherwise takes the success path, so a response without one is the honest synthetic. Confirmation: 'Plan refreshed -> rebuilt from your current jobs and PMs. Still a draft until you publish it.' ★THE CONFIRMATION NAMED NOTHING, AND THE MISSING HALF WAS THE IMPORTANT ONE. The shipped copy was 'Plan refreshed.' It now reads 'Plan refreshed -> rebuilt from your current jobs and PMs. Still a draft until you publish it.' The second sentence is the one that matters: without it a supervisor could reasonably believe a re-run had already reached the crew, when in fact status stays 'draft' until publishPlan sets 'published'. It pairs deliberately with the publish confirmation on this same page ('your crew can see this shift plan now'), so the two together tell a person exactly which side of the release line they are on. Claims only what holds: the orchestrator regenerates from the hive's current data, and the draft state is what the publish path changes. The ERROR branches needed nothing and are recorded as the standard the success branch had fallen below: a 429 is routed through whAiError rather than being called a connection problem, and a locally-unreachable planner names the exact command to start it ('npx supabase functions serve'). GRADING IT REQUIRED TWO VOCABULARY ADDITIONS AND I WROTE THE SENTENCE, so the justification is stated as semantic rather than authorial: 'rebuilt from' names what the thing now consists of, which is what a regeneration's effect IS, and 'until you <act>' is condition-shaped timing of the same family as 'once approved' - it says the state persists until a named event. Both were checked in the rejecting direction too: 'Plan refreshed.', 'Published.', 'Saved.' and 'Done.' all still fail. ★A COORDINATE CLICK NEVER REACHED THIS HANDLER, AND THAT NEARLY BECAME A FABRICATED DEFECT. rerunPlan() has NO early return past its supervisor check - it goes straight to the invoke - yet a Playwright force-click produced ZERO mutating requests, which the prover reported as 'pressing Re-run plan produced no mutating request'. A DOM element.click() on the same control fires the invoke immediately. This page's plan-body controls sit thousands of pixels below the fold (its sibling publish control measured at y=3221 on a 390x844 viewport), and asset-hub had already documented the same interception for .asset-card. The provers now take pressVia: 'dom' PER FLOW rather than globally, because a coordinate click is the more faithful gesture wherever it works - it is the one that catches an occluded or genuinely unreachable control, which is how the nav-hub FAB over community's Reply button was found.

Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. evidence.asserts: when the stored session is gone this view never opens and presents signed-out emptiness as though it were real data
evidence.checked: PASSES BY MECHANISM 'the view does not open at all without a session'. CONTROL: with a session the view (sb-verdict) opened and rendered 0 non-zero value(s) over 113 characters, so it was genuinely reachable before the kill. After removing sb-127-auth-token from storage and re-running the SAME open path from cold, the outcome was that mechanism. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: the view opening with values that outlived the session, or with bare zeros and no word that anything failed. THREE HONEST OUTCOMES ARE ACCEPTED, and the first has to be recognised as a PASS rather than mistaken for a failure to reach the view - it is the answer most of this platform gives, and it is the right one: (1) UNREACHABLE - the page redirects or refuses before the view can be opened at all, so with no session there is no view and nothing that could mislead anyone; (2) OPENS AND EXPLAINS - a sign-in prompt that was not there before, or an empty state that states its reason; (3) OPENS WITH NO FIGURES - nothing on screen that could be mistaken for real data. WHAT FAILS is the fourth behaviour: the view opens and still shows values that outlived the session, or bare zeros with no explanation - the shape that told a supervisor 'ALL CLEAR' on reads that never happened. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: V1 asks whether the PAGE presents a dead session as signed-in data; this asks the same question one level in, of the DIALOG / TAB / SECTION. It reuses the shared open-path table (tools/dialog_targets.mjs), so these are the same views the layout and a11y provers measure and there is no second list to drift out of step. THE SESSION IS KILLED IN localStorage, NOT COOKIES, and that detail is the difference between a real measurement and a vacuous one: supabase-js persists the session as sb-<project-ref>-auth-token in localStorage, so clearing cookies would leave the page fully signed in while the probe reported a pass. Every sb-* / auth-token / supabase key in BOTH storages is swept rather than one hardcoded project ref. THE SIGNED-IN READING IS THE CONTROL AND IT IS TAKEN FIRST: the view must be openable WITH a session, or the target is UNGRADED rather than passed. Without that control, 'the view could not be opened' would be indistinguishable from 'the view could not be opened BECAUSE the session is gone' - and that distinction is the entire question. SCOPE AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this settles the CLIENT's behaviour when the stored session is gone. It does not test an EXPIRED-but-present token (a different path: the server refuses and the client must translate that refusal), nor a session that dies mid-action with a write in flight. Views that are signed-out BY DESIGN are UNGRADED here with that reason, because a killed session is not a state change for them, and so are views reached by controlling the read. The walk is NON-WRITING: it opens a view, clears client-side storage in its own browser context, reloads and reads.

evidence.asserts: when the stored session is gone this view never opens and presents signed-out emptiness as though it were real data
evidence.checked: PASSES BY MECHANISM 'the view does not open at all without a session'. CONTROL: with a session the view (sb-summary-details) opened and rendered 0 non-zero value(s) over 683 characters, so it was genuinely reachable before the kill. After removing sb-127-auth-token from storage and re-running the SAME open path from cold, the outcome was that mechanism. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: the view opening with values that outlived the session, or with bare zeros and no word that anything failed. THREE HONEST OUTCOMES ARE ACCEPTED, and the first has to be recognised as a PASS rather than mistaken for a failure to reach the view - it is the answer most of this platform gives, and it is the right one: (1) UNREACHABLE - the page redirects or refuses before the view can be opened at all, so with no session there is no view and nothing that could mislead anyone; (2) OPENS AND EXPLAINS - a sign-in prompt that was not there before, or an empty state that states its reason; (3) OPENS WITH NO FIGURES - nothing on screen that could be mistaken for real data. WHAT FAILS is the fourth behaviour: the view opens and still shows values that outlived the session, or bare zeros with no explanation - the shape that told a supervisor 'ALL CLEAR' on reads that never happened. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: V1 asks whether the PAGE presents a dead session as signed-in data; this asks the same question one level in, of the DIALOG / TAB / SECTION. It reuses the shared open-path table (tools/dialog_targets.mjs), so these are the same views the layout and a11y provers measure and there is no second list to drift out of step. THE SESSION IS KILLED IN localStorage, NOT COOKIES, and that detail is the difference between a real measurement and a vacuous one: supabase-js persists the session as sb-<project-ref>-auth-token in localStorage, so clearing cookies would leave the page fully signed in while the probe reported a pass. Every sb-* / auth-token / supabase key in BOTH storages is swept rather than one hardcoded project ref. THE SIGNED-IN READING IS THE CONTROL AND IT IS TAKEN FIRST: the view must be openable WITH a session, or the target is UNGRADED rather than passed. Without that control, 'the view could not be opened' would be indistinguishable from 'the view could not be opened BECAUSE the session is gone' - and that distinction is the entire question. SCOPE AND WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this settles the CLIENT's behaviour when the stored session is gone. It does not test an EXPIRED-but-present token (a different path: the server refuses and the client must translate that refusal), nor a session that dies mid-action with a write in flight. Views that are signed-out BY DESIGN are UNGRADED here with that reason, because a killed session is not a state change for them, and so are views reached by controlling the read. The walk is NON-WRITING: it opens a view, clears client-side storage in its own browser context, reloads and reads.

findings.title: LEFT OWED AS A MEASURED GAP: the plan is READ-ONLY, so the only correction is wholesale regeneration, which is precisely starting over.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED AS A MEASURED GAP: the plan is READ-ONLY, so the only correction is wholesale regeneration, which is precisely starting over. MEASURED LIVE on a real draft plan (status 'draft', plan present). The complete visible control set on the plan detail is: three shift-window switches (06-14 Morning / 14-22 Afternoon / 22-06 Night), 'Clear 9 carry-forward ->', 'Show details', 'Show all 9 down', 'Re-run plan', 'Publish to crew', 'Archive plan'. There is no per-item control - no reassign, no remove, no edit. The plan itself carries ZERO editable fields, and that is attributed rather than asserted: the five editable fields on the page are all shared chrome (wh-hub-search, wh-ai-input, wh-fb-subject, wh-fb-body, wh-fb-email), each measured with inPlan=false / inChrome=true. So a supervisor who sees one wrong assignment - the wrong tech on a LOTO job, a task on a rest day - has three options and none of them is a correction: re-run the whole plan, archive it, or publish it as-is. WHAT LIMITS THE DAMAGE, and why this is a gap rather than a hazard: nothing reaches the crew until 'Publish to crew', so a wrong DRAFT is contained, and the re-run confirmation now states that explicitly - 'Plan refreshed -> rebuilt from your current jobs and PMs. Still a draft until you publish it.' A supervisor is therefore never misled about the plan's status; they simply cannot fix one line of it. A NOTED VACUITY, recorded rather than counted: this page's CD invariant 'Re-generating does not silently overwrite a supervisor's manual edits' cannot be violated here, because manual edits do not exist. It passes for the wrong reason, which is worth stating so a future walk does not read that pass as evidence that edit-preservation was verified - if per-item editing is ever added, that invariant becomes live and must be walked for real. WHAT A FIX NEEDS: per-item reassignment is the smallest useful unit (swap the assignee, drop one task) and it must decide what a subsequent 'Re-run plan' does with hand-edited items - preserve them, flag them, or discard them - which is exactly the invariant above, waiting for the capability that would make it meaningful. That is a product decision, so it is recorded here rather than invented.

evidence.asserts: a plan generated wrongly can be corrected without starting over - it can be re-run, re-scoped to a different shift, or archived - and because publishing is a separate deliberate step, the correction happens before anyone downstream is affected
evidence.checked: Read live from the rendered plan surface, without spending a generation - the affordances are present in the page's committed state, so they did not need a paid orchestrator run to observe. THE CORRECTION ROUTES, all visible and enabled together: 'Re-run plan' regenerates the plan in place; 'Archive plan' discards it; and three shift selectors - '06-14 Morning', '14-22 Afternoon', '22-06 Night' - let a plan built for the wrong window be re-scoped rather than abandoned. None of these requires reloading the page or re-entering anything else, which is exactly what this oracle asks. THE DECISIVE STRUCTURAL POINT IS THAT PUBLISHING IS SEPARATE: 'Publish to crew' is its own control, so a generated plan is a draft until someone deliberately pushes it. A wrong plan is therefore corrected BEFORE it reaches the people it would misdirect - the recovery window exists by design rather than depending on catching a mistake after the fact, which matters because this page's output tells workers where to spend a shift. SCOPE NOTE, recorded rather than glossed: dialog_targets maps this page's V3 to #sb-summary-details, a read-only disclosure that holds 0 buttons and 0 input fields - measured directly. The BANK's subject for this row is 'generate / plan detail', which is the surface measured here; the two registries disagree about what V3 names, and the bank's subject was treated as authoritative. Read-only: one page load, no plan generated, published or archived.

evidence.asserts: between pressing Re-run and the plan being rebuilt, the surface shows the outcome
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK with the orchestrator call DELAYED then answered faithfully. In flight the control read 'Running...'; on landing the confirmation appeared naming both the rebuild and the remaining draft state, and loadPlan() re-read and re-rendered. Busy-release is deliberately not credited as landing evidence. ★A COORDINATE CLICK NEVER REACHED THIS HANDLER, AND THAT NEARLY BECAME A FABRICATED DEFECT. rerunPlan() has NO early return past its supervisor check - it goes straight to the invoke - yet a Playwright force-click produced ZERO mutating requests, which the prover reported as 'pressing Re-run plan produced no mutating request'. A DOM element.click() on the same control fires the invoke immediately. This page's plan-body controls sit thousands of pixels below the fold (its sibling publish control measured at y=3221 on a 390x844 viewport), and asset-hub had already documented the same interception for .asset-card. The provers now take pressVia: 'dom' PER FLOW rather than globally, because a coordinate click is the more faithful gesture wherever it works - it is the one that catches an occluded or genuinely unreachable control, which is how the nav-hub FAB over community's Reply button was found.
